questions.question: A coder agent publishes task.code.done instead of calling the reviewer directly. What does the coder no longer need to know?
options: The payload format that the event must follow
The name of the topic that the event is sent to
Whether its own task finished or failed
Which agents react to the event, or how many
questions.explanation: This is space decoupling. The publisher still owns the topic name and the payload schema, but it does not know the subscribers.

questions.question: Using the lesson's wildcard rules, which topic does the pattern task.*.done match?
options: task.code.failed, since * covers the last token
task.research.done, since * covers one token
task.done, since * may also match zero tokens
task.code.review.done, since * covers two tokens
questions.explanation: The * wildcard matches exactly one token. The > wildcard is the one that matches one or more tokens, and only at the end.

questions.question: Audit and billing must each see every event. Two reviewers should split the review work. How do you subscribe them?
options: All four consumers as members of one shared subscription
Four separate subscriptions, one for each consumer
Audit and billing separate; both reviewers in one subscription
Audit and billing in one subscription; reviewers separate
questions.explanation: Separate subscriptions fan out, so each gets a copy. Members of one subscription compete, so each message goes to only one of them.

questions.question: Why does at-least-once delivery produce duplicate messages?
options: The broker cannot tell a lost ack from unprocessed work
The broker sends each message to every group member
The publisher retries when no subscriber has matched
The routing key hashes two messages to one consumer
questions.explanation: If the work is done but the acknowledgement is lost, the broker sees only silence and must redeliver. An idempotent consumer absorbs the repeat.

questions.question: In the demo, message 5 was dead-lettered by review, yet audit and billing handled it normally. Why?
options: The broker deletes a message once any group nacks it
Each subscription has its own queue and fails alone
Audit and billing received it before review nacked
The routing key sent it only to the review group
questions.explanation: Fan-out gives each subscription an independent copy with its own delivery attempts. One subscriber's failure does not affect the others.

questions.question: The broker retries a failed message at the front of its queue. What does this choice trade?
options: It keeps order but lets a bad message block the rest
It avoids duplicates but loses messages on a crash
It spreads load evenly but breaks per-key ordering
It raises throughput but removes the delivery limit
questions.explanation: Retrying before moving on preserves order and causes head-of-line blocking. The delivery limit and dead-letter queue bound how long the block lasts.
